addedLines: - claude: Catch-all for any task that doesn't fit a more specific agent. FleetView's default when no agent name is typed. (Tools: *)

- codex:codex-rescue: Proactively use when Claude Code is stuck, wants a second implementation or diagnosis pass, needs a deeper root-cause investigation, or should hand a substantial coding task to Codex through the shared runtime (Tools: Bash)

- Explore: Read-only search agent for broad fan-out searches — when answering means sweeping many files, directories, or naming conventions and you only need the conclusion, not the file dumps. It reads excerpts rather than whole files, so it locates code; it doesn't review or audit it. Specify search breadth: "medium" for moderate exploration, "very thorough" for multiple locations and naming conventions. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)

- general-purpose: General-purpose agent for researching complex questions, searching for code, and executing multi-step tasks. When you are searching for a keyword or file and are not confident that you will find the right match in the first few tries use this agent to perform the search for you. (Tools: *)

- Plan: Software architect agent for designing implementation plans. Use this when you need to plan the implementation strategy for a task. Returns step-by-step plans, identifies critical files, and considers architectural trade-offs. (Tools: All tools except Agent, Artifact, ArtifactComments, ArtifactData, ArtifactCheck, ExitPlanMode, Edit, Write, NotebookEdit)
- statusline-setup: Use this agent to configure the user's Claude Code status line setting. (Tools: Read, Edit)

- zeroh-roadmap:arc-eval-judge: Scores a LANDED arc's judge-owned eval dimensions (standards adherence, doc brevity, composability/testability, plan quality) from its recorded trace and diff, returning a typed ArcEvalJudgeVerdict with quoted evidence. Spawned by do-arc's eval step and the eval-arc skill; never recomputes a deterministic signal. (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, Bash)

- zeroh-roadmap:code-reviewer: Reviews code for bugs, logic errors, pattern adherence, and business rule correctness using confidence-based filtering to report only high-priority issues (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, Edit, Write, Bash, WebFetch, WebSearch, TodoWrite, LSP)

- zeroh-roadmap:intent-validator: Independent intent judge — drives the real shipped flow at one acceptance criterion's tier, captures concrete evidence, scores fulfilled intent against a rubric, and returns a typed IntentVerdict. Spawned by validate-arc, one per criterion; never grades work it built. (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, Bash, WebFetch, WebSearch, TodoWrite)

- zeroh-roadmap:phase-executor: Runs do-phase for ONE phase end-to-end inside an arc and returns a structured PhaseExecutionResult. Spawned by the do-arc orchestrator; never user-invoked. (Tools: All tools)

- zeroh-roadmap:quality-pass: One-shot end-of-phase quality sweep — the merged architect-critique + simplifier pass. Additive half fixes shortcuts, hardcodes, cross-task patterns, and neighborhood issues in touched files; subtractive half deletes dead scaffolding, speculative abstractions, and noise. Auto-fixes in scope; hard-stops on multi-repo / scoped-out / product / speculative. Runs once per phase (reviewScope full only), before the code-review loop. (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, Edit, Write, Bash, WebFetch, WebSearch, TodoWrite, LSP)
- zeroh-roadmap:references:executor-reference: Agent from zeroh-roadmap plugin (Tools: All tools)

- zeroh-roadmap:software-architect: Designs system architecture by analyzing existing patterns, making decisive technical choices, and producing implementation blueprints. Also the architecture advisor for plan-arc's design-first gate — searches the consumer's arch docs and recommends reuse-or-design (a search-and-recommend role, distinct from the compromise-breaking Decision Contract). (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, Bash, WebFetch, WebSearch, LSP)

- zeroh-roadmap:software-developer: Implements features by understanding existing patterns, writing clean code, and following project conventions with a focus on maintainability (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, Edit, Write, Bash, WebFetch, WebSearch, TodoWrite, LSP)

- zeroh-roadmap:test-engineer: Writes behavioral unit tests that catch real regressions, enforces coverage on executable logic, and validates that business rules are tested (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, Edit, Write, Bash, WebFetch, TodoWrite, LSP)

- zeroh-roadmap:ux-designer: Senior UX design role — designs a surface's layout within the consumer's own UX standards BEFORE it is built, decides per arc whether prose layout reasoning or a static HTML preview is warranted, and returns a recommended UX designRef for the user to confirm. Spawned by plan-arc's design-first gate's UX sub-gate (Step 1b) when an arc has a surface. (Tools: Glob, Grep, Read, Write, Edit, Bash, WebFetch, WebSearch)

- eli5: Explain any topic, code, concept, or error tailored to a specific audience's level of understanding. Use this skill whenever the user says 'explain like I am', 'ELI5', 'explain this to my', 'break this down for', 'dumb it down', 'simplify this for', or asks you to explain something to a specific person or audience type (e.g., 'explain this to a manager', 'how would I explain this to my mom', 'make this understandable for a 5th grader'). Also trigger when the user mentions wanting to understand something at a particular level, or asks for an explanation targeting a non-technical audience. Even partial matches like 'explain to my wife' or 'tell my boss' should trigger this skill.
- goal: Receive and execute a goal dispatched by the lead sentinel (a message beginning with /goal). Acknowledge, plan and execute via the roadmap system, and report halts and landings to the lead by appending a line to your own inbox — the done-report is what pops the lead's queue.
- lead-sentinel: Operate as the fleet's lead sentinel — the voice-connected manager session that dispatches goals to worker sessions, monitors their state, reviews their work, and reports to the owner. Use when this session is the Viky voice brain or the owner asks for fleet status, dispatch, nudge, review of other sessions' work, or what the fleet should work on next.
- codex:rescue: Delegate investigation, an explicit fix request, or follow-up rescue work to the Codex rescue subagent
- codex:setup: Check whether the local Codex CLI is ready and optionally toggle the stop-time review gate
- zeroh-greenfield:brownfield-audit: Handle requests phrased as audit, fill gaps, or reconcile an established repository by proposing only missing, partial, or stale homes before approval.
- zeroh-greenfield:greenfield-init: Handle requests phrased as initialize, scaffold, or create a new repository through an approval-gated setup with sourced stack, design, standards, and roadmap pointers.
- zeroh-greenfield:stack-decision: Handle requests phrased as choose stack, mobile stack, or compare frameworks by presenting sourced alternatives without defaults and returning an ADR ruling.
- zeroh-greenfield:using-zeroh-greenfield: Route requests phrased as init, scaffold, brownfield audit, fill gaps, or stack choice to the owning zeroh-greenfield skill.
- zeroh-roadmap:arc-sweep: Pre-merge sweep for a built arc: dispose every accumulated compromise (reusing release-sweep's debt vocabulary) and run one whole-arc software-architect review against the arc's singleSeams + designRefs, then report merge-readiness.
- zeroh-roadmap:audit-roadmap: Read-only structural audit across roadmap state and the vendored schema (17 checks). Reports findings only — never fixes.
- zeroh-roadmap:do-arc: Execute a whole arc end to end: launch one per-plane workflow at a time, own the halts it hands back, sweep + validate in-session, and land via the CLI.
- zeroh-roadmap:do-phase: Execute a roadmap phase task-by-task with enforced sequential discipline: one task = one commit + a transparencyReport, then the kind-selected gate.
- zeroh-roadmap:eval-arc: Score a landed arc across the seven ratified dimensions — code confidence, verified-vs-intent, standards adherence, doc brevity, composability/testability, speed, plan quality — into a typed, dated ArcEvalReport ratcheted against a rolling baseline. The standalone door onto do-arc's Step 9, for arcs that landed without it.
- zeroh-roadmap:full-code-review: Whole-codebase pre-release audit. Parallel agents cover security, dead code, duplication, performance, architecture, edge cases, data flow, and domain-critical calculations; findings become a release verdict (any critical blocks), a remediation phase, and a review-record round. Use for "full code review", "pre-release audit", a pre-prod checkup on worry areas, or before merge-to-main/prod deploy. Not this skill: diff/phase review (code-review); a consumer's own release-review supersedes this.
- zeroh-roadmap:handoff: Routes unfinished session context into durable roadmap artifacts, leaving only justified residue for a fresh session. Use for requests to hand off work, hand off to a fresh session, continue in a new session, write a context file, or produce a one-line prompt.
- zeroh-roadmap:plan-arc: Plan a whole arc (a named, contiguous block of phases shipped as one unit): author the Arc entity, resolve the design-first gate WITH the user (reuse / new design / inherited ratified prototype / recorded skip), plan every member phase against that design, review each independently, queue one arc tier. Triggers: 'plan arc', '/plan-arc', 'create arc', 'new arc'. Not this skill: one standalone phase (plan-phase) or executing an existing arc (do-arc).
- zeroh-roadmap:plan-phase: Create a new roadmap phase. Use when user says: create phase, plan phase, add to roadmap, new phase, add feature, create task. Reads the code first, pre-makes every decision, rehearses verifies in both directions, then writes and commits a .phase.ts file. Not this skill: planning a multi-phase arc (plan-arc, which loops plan-phase per member) or queueing/auditing an existing phase (review-phase owns the queue).
- zeroh-roadmap:release-sweep: Review and resolve outstanding debts for a release version, then optionally archive the version's done phases. Run before every minor/major; optional before patches. Patch releases are never blocked on debts; archive is.
- zeroh-roadmap:review-phase: Independently verify a roadmap phase or whole arc against the real code: backlog phases get a plan-quality review that repairs the plan and queues it; done/in-progress phases get a report-only post-execution audit. Trigger: 'review phase N', '/review-phase N', 'verify/audit phase N', 'review arc <ID>'; also the mandatory pre-queue pass after plan-phase and the spawned judge step in plan-arc. Not for general diff/PR review or bug hunting - that is a plain diff review (the code-reviewer agent).
- zeroh-roadmap:test-strategy: Test pyramid, coverage targets, and conventions. Use when writing tests, reviewing test quality, or planning test phases.
- zeroh-roadmap:using-zeroh-roadmap: ALWAYS ACTIVE. Phase-driven development plugin. MUST be used when user says: create phase, plan phase, do phase, roadmap, review phase, code review, what's next, arc, sweep, backlog. Routes ALL development task requests through the phase system.
- zeroh-roadmap:validate-arc: Drive a built arc's real shipped flow and judge it against its acceptance criteria with an independent judge panel, reporting PASS/GAPS. The terminal intent gate do-arc runs after arc-sweep, before merge.
- codex:codex-cli-runtime: Internal helper contract for calling the codex-companion runtime from Claude Code
- codex:codex-result-handling: Internal guidance for presenting Codex helper output back to the user
- codex:gpt-5-4-prompting: Internal guidance for composing Codex and GPT-5.4 prompts for coding, review, diagnosis, and research tasks inside the Codex Claude Code plugin
- dataviz: Use this skill whenever you are about to create ANY chart, graph, plot, dashboard, or data visualization, in ANY output medium — an HTML or React artifact, inline SVG, plotting code in any library (matplotlib, plotly, d3, Recharts, …), an image/PNG you will render and upload, or a chart shared into Slack. Read it BEFORE writing the first line of chart code, choosing chart colors, building a stat tile / meter / KPI row, or laying out a dashboard. When the destination is a first-party document connector (host-designated, never self-described) that renders live charts, hand it the rows (inline, or as an uploaded data file the chart cites) rather than a rendered PNG/SVG — a picture of a chart loses hover, data inspection and per-value comments. Produces visualizations that read as one system — elegant, accessible, consistent in light and dark — using a brand-neutral placeholder palette you swap for your own. Teaches a design-system-agnostic method: a form heuristic, a color formula with a runnable validator, mark specs, and interaction rules. A validated default palette is documented in `references/palette.md` — swap that file's values for your brand's. Triggers on: "chart", "graph", "plot", "data viz", "visualization", "dashboard", "analytics", "visualize data", "categorical colors", "sequential / diverging palette", "stat tile", "sparkline", "heatmap", "legend", "axis", "tooltip", "chart colors", "color by series".
- update-config: Use this skill to configure the Claude Code harness via settings.json. Automated behaviors ("from now on when X", "each time X", "whenever X", "before/after X") require hooks configured in settings.json - the harness executes these, not Claude, so memory/preferences cannot fulfill them. Also use for: permissions ("allow X", "add permission", "move permission to"), env vars ("set X=Y"), hook troubleshooting, or any changes to settings.json/settings.local.json files. Examples: "allow npm commands", "add bq permission to global settings", "move permission to user settings", "set DEBUG=true", "when claude stops show X". For simple settings like theme/model, suggest the /config command.
- keybindings-help: Use when the user wants to customize keyboard shortcuts, rebind keys, add chord bindings, or modify ~/.claude/keybindings.json. Examples: "rebind ctrl+s", "add a chord shortcut", "change the submit key", "customize keybindings".
- code-review: Review the current diff, or a PR number/branch/path target, for correctness bugs and reuse/simplification/efficiency cleanups at the given effort level (low/medium: fewer, high-confidence findings; high→max: broader coverage, may include uncertain findings; ultra: deep multi-agent review in the cloud); with no level given, it reuses the level you typed last. Pass --comment to post findings as inline PR comments, or --fix to apply the findings to the working tree after the review. For ultra on a GitHub.com PR target, --post asks to post the finished review’s findings to the PR as a single comment from the user’s GitHub account (not a review; the launch dialog still confirms in interactive sessions, while non-interactive mode posts on the flag alone) and --no-post hides that option.
- simplify: Review the changed code for reuse, simplification, efficiency, and altitude cleanups, then apply the fixes. Quality only — it does not hunt for bugs; use /code-review for that.

# Using zeroh-greenfield

Inspect the repository before choosing exactly one route; return the dispatch contract below and do not execute the routed workflow.
Not this skill: delegate routed work to `greenfield-init`, `brownfield-audit`, or `stack-decision`; keep only initial trigger routing here. Use `roadmap/arc-evals/phase-29.peval.json` as the 2026-09-04 delivery evidence.

## Dispatch

| Request | Skill |
| --- | --- |
| init / new repo / scaffold | greenfield-init |
| audit / fill gaps / brownfield | brownfield-audit |
| stack choice / mobile stack | stack-decision |

Return exactly one object:

```json
{"route":"greenfield-init|brownfield-audit|stack-decision","evidence":["<repository-relative-path>"]}
```

Define `<repository-relative-path>` as an inspected marker path. If inspection cannot resolve the repository root, STOP with `route: unresolved` and the attempted path; this STOP is honor-system.

## Detection markers

Treat any existing marker as brownfield evidence. When markers disagree, use
`brownfield-audit`; it preserves existing homes and proposes only gaps.
Apply the canonical detection procedure in `../brownfield-audit/references/marker-table.md`; its root resolver refusal enforces ambiguous-root failure, while route selection remains honor-system.

| Marker | Greenfield | Brownfield |
| --- | --- | --- |
| package-manager locks | absent | one or more present |
| framework files | absent | framework config or source present |
| existing docs | absent | product, architecture, UX, or standards docs present |
| harness files | absent | AGENTS.md, CLAUDE.md, or another agent harness present |
| roadmap config | no marked root | canonical resolver finds a marked root or config (see `../brownfield-audit/references/marker-table.md`) |

## Ownership boundaries

- Delegate post-initialization phase planning and execution to `zeroh-roadmap`; prepare only the consumer homes and pointers it needs.
- Delegate Blade tokens, themes, and branded design work to `zeroh-design`; record only its pointers.
- Keep the trigger map in this router. Treat both ownership rules as honor-system; each routed skill names this router as the reverse boundary.

name: greenfield-init
description: Handle requests phrased as initialize, scaffold, or create a new repository through an approval-gated setup with sourced stack, design, standards, and roadmap pointers.
---

# Greenfield initialization

Use this workflow only after `using-zeroh-greenfield` finds no brownfield
markers. Load each reference only at the step that names it.
Not this skill: route initial trigger selection through `using-zeroh-greenfield`, repositories with existing markers through `brownfield-audit`, and alternative selection through `stack-decision`. Use `roadmap/arc-evals/phase-32.peval.json` as the 2026-09-04 initialized-home evidence.

## Read-only compatibility preflight

Before the interview, proposal, approval request, generator, or any consumer write,
require `roadmap` and run `roadmap config capabilities --json`. The response must be
valid JSON with `configVersion: 1`, `scopeManifestProtocol:
"scope-manifest-json-v1"`, and slots `unit-scoped`, `unit-affected`, and
`unit-impacted`. If the command is absent, exits nonzero, returns malformed or older
capabilities, print `/plugin install zeroh-roadmap@zeroh-marketplace` and STOP with
zero consumer writes.
Before approval, run only that named roadmap command; specifically do not invoke `roadmap init`, including `roadmap init --help`. The CLI command-help dispatch keeps `roadmap init --help` read-only; `plugins/zeroh-roadmap/test/fixture-consumer/greenfield-live-evidence.test.mjs` later rejects any observed preapproval mutation.

## Interview

Load `references/prd-interview.md`. Ask one question at a time and retain
unknowns. Do not write the PRD yet.

Invoke `zeroh-greenfield:stack-decision` after the platforms and constraints
are known. It owns the stack alternatives and decision-record text.

## Draft proposal

Load these references in order and assemble a complete proposal:

1. `references/design-system.md` for the design-system choice or sibling handoff.
2. `references/archetypes/<name>.md` for the chosen generator and file shape, where `<name>` is `web`, `flutter`, `android`, `expo`, `nx-monorepo`, or `library-cli`.
3. `references/standards.md` for repository conventions and documentation.

Present every proposed operation in this exact table:

| Artifact | Target | Reason |
| --- | --- | --- |
| <artifact-or-command> | <consumer-path> | <why-it-is-needed> |

Include generator commands as artifacts. Cover the PRD,
decision records, design pointers, archetype, standards, harness files, README,
and roadmap configuration before requesting approval.

Also emit this parser-bound object with concrete values and exactly the seven gate keys:

```json
{"type":"proposal","artifacts":[{"path":"<repository-relative-path>","reason":"<reason>"}],"commands":[{"command":"<command>"}],"gates":{"lint":"<command-or-none>","types":"<command-or-none>","unit":"<command-or-none>","integration":"<command-or-none>","build":"<command-or-none>","e2e":"<command-or-none>","emit":"<command-or-none>"}}
```

Define paths relative to the consumer root, reasons as non-empty approval rationale, and `none` as an approved absence with its reason in the proposal table. `plugins/zeroh-roadmap/test/fixture-consumer/greenfield-live-evidence.test.mjs` rejects unsafe, broad, duplicate, or unproposed artifact paths.

## Approval gate

Ask for the exact response `APPROVE GREENFIELD PLAN`.

STOP before any write or generator run unless that exact response follows the
complete proposal. Do not interpret partial agreement as approval. Record the
approved plan and response in `docs/PRD.md §Decisions` during execution.
Treat this gate as enforced by `plugins/zeroh-roadmap/test/fixture-consumer/greenfield-live-evidence.test.mjs`; other approval interpretation is honor-system.

If a Blade brand requires the design sibling and it is absent, show
`/plugin install zeroh-design@zeroh-marketplace` and STOP that branch. Do not
substitute either sibling's work.

## Execute approved plan

Execute only approved rows through the following headings in order. Run the selected archetype generator first, then write the PRD, decision records, standards, architecture and UX indexes, and harness adapters.

## Structure

Populate README structure from the selected manifest's `## File tree` and
approved `## Generator` and `## Post-steps` outputs.

## Commands

Populate README commands from the selected manifest’s `## Verify` and test conventions.
Resolve `templates/scripts/check-readme-catalog.mjs` from the installed zeroh-greenfield plugin root, copy it to consumer path `scripts/check-readme-catalog.mjs`, and run the selected manifest checker.
Record its exit code before Done.


## Roadmap configuration

Run `roadmap init`, then apply only the keys from `references/pointers.md`.

Never replace an existing home discovered after approval. Stop with the changed
evidence and draft a revised proposal instead.

## Verify

Follow `references/pointers.md` to execute every non-`none` gate from the consumer root, recording cwd/exit and approved absence reasons. Run the selected archetype's Verify command, the README catalog check, and
`roadmap config check`. Report each command and exit status. A failing command
keeps the initialization incomplete.

## Done

Return Done only when every approved artifact exists, every unapproved path is unchanged,
the approval ruling is in the PRD, the catalog check passes, and
`roadmap config check` exits `0`. Report the artifact paths and verification
results; do not use a prose-only success claim.

After auditing the completed tree, emit `{"type":"audit-result","proposals":[],"writes":[],"gaps":[]}` only when the skill proposes and writes nothing. `plugins/zeroh-roadmap/test/fixture-consumer/greenfield-live-evidence.test.mjs` later cross-checks the claim against independent observer events and tree snapshots; treat other STOP and preservation instructions as honor-system.
=====
## Generator
```sh
npx create-vite@^8 my-lib --template vanilla-ts
```

Source: https://vite.dev/guide/. Vite is MIT, tier `Allowed anywhere`.

## Post-steps
Install `tsup: ^8.5` and `@types/node`, and include `node` in the TypeScript
`types` list. tsup is sourced from https://tsup.egoist.dev/; it is MIT and
`Allowed anywhere`. Set package.json `exports` to `./dist/index.js`, `bin` to
`./dist/cli.js`, and `files` to `dist`. Configure `tsup.config.ts` with
`entry: ['src/index.ts', 'src/cli.ts']`, `format: ['esm']`, and `dts: true`.
Set the package.json `build` script to `tsup`.
Give the CLI a Node shebang and a stable `--help` path. Add at least one
`node:test` file for the public API, then run the tsup build before Verify.

## File tree
```text
my-lib/
my-lib/package.json
my-lib/src/index.ts
my-lib/src/cli.ts
my-lib/tsup.config.ts
```

## Conventions delta
Keep the reusable API in `src/index.ts` and the thin executable adapter in
`src/cli.ts`; publish only built artifacts through `exports`, `bin`, and `files`.

## testConventions
Use `node --test` for behavior and `node dist/cli.js --help` as the built CLI
smoke check. Test runner source: https://nodejs.org/api/test.html.

## designHomes
Set `designHomes.architecture.home` to `docs/architecture.md` and
`designHomes.ux.canon` to `docs/ux-canon.md`.

## Verify
```sh
test -f my-lib/package.json && test -f my-lib/src/index.ts && test -f my-lib/src/cli.ts && test -f my-lib/tsup.config.ts && (cd my-lib && npm run build && node --test && node dist/cli.js --help && node scripts/check-readme-catalog.mjs --project-root .)
```

# Archetype manifest contract

## Generator
One fenced block containing a literal generator command.

## Post-steps
Exact approved edits after generation.

## File tree
One fenced, non-empty two-level tree.

## Conventions delta
Only archetype-specific additions to the shared conventions.

## testConventions
At least two literal commands or patterns.

## designHomes
The architecture and UX pointers consumed by the roadmap.

## Verify
Exactly one fenced, single-line exit-code command. Keep observations and dates
only in `VERIFY-RECORD-2026-09.md`.
=====
## Tool gate
The skill's first preflight must prove `scope-manifest-json-v1` plus scoped,
affected, and impacted slots before this reference is used.

## Config branch
Use the canonical discovery procedure in `skills/brownfield-audit/references/marker-table.md` to locate the resolved root before testing configuration presence. If its config is absent, propose `roadmap init`; if present, never run init. Merge only approved missing keys. Existing keys are preserved unless an individually approved stale/partial repair names the old value, replacement, and evidence. Never create a second config at the repository top level.

## Bind and prove commands
The tables are proposal inputs, not proof that a generator installed a runner.
Before approval, inspect the generated or existing package scripts, test files,
Gradle tasks, and tool availability. Propose installation/configuration of missing
promised runners and at least one meaningful test. Never bind `npm test` or
Playwright without that setup. A slot with no applicable tooling is explicitly
`none` (declared absent), with a recorded reason approved in the proposal; absence
is not a passing test. Never downgrade an existing or promised test to `none` to
make verification green. Replace candidate bindings with the repository's actual
commands where needed and retain their source evidence.
Execute every non-`none` gate from the consumer project root after approval and
record its command, cwd, and exit. STOP on failure or unavailable tooling; config
validation alone does not prove executability. Re-run after a binding changes.

## Merge manifest pointers
Copy only the selected manifest values into `designHomes.architecture.home`, `designHomes.architecture.extendProtocol`, `designHomes.ux.canon`, `designHomes.ux.qualityExemplar`, `designHomes.ux.copyRules`, `designHomes.ux.bindingDesignSystem`, and `testConventions`.

##### templates/scripts/check-readme-catalog.mjs
#!/usr/bin/env node
import { existsSync, readFileSync } from 'node:fs'
import { basename, resolve } from 'node:path'

const args = process.argv.slice(2)
if (args.includes('--help')) {
  console.log('Usage: check-readme-catalog.mjs (--catalog <json> | --project-root <dir>) [--readme <file>]')
  process.exit(0)
}
const value = flag => { const i = args.indexOf(flag); return i >= 0 ? args[i + 1] : undefined }
const readmePath = resolve(value('--readme') ?? 'README.md')
const fail = message => { console.error(message); process.exitCode = 1 }
if (!existsSync(readmePath)) fail(`nonexistent README: ${readmePath}`)
else {
  const body = readFileSync(readmePath, 'utf8')
  const block = body.match(/<!-- repo-catalog:start -->([\s\S]*?)<!-- repo-catalog:end -->/)?.[1]
  if (!block) fail('malformed README catalog')
  else {
    const tableLines = block.split(/\r?\n/).filter(line => line.trim().startsWith('|'))
    const parsedRows = [...block.matchAll(/^\|\s*([^|]+?)\s*\|\s*([^|]+?)\s*\|\s*([^|]*?)\s*\|$/gm)]
    if (parsedRows.length !== tableLines.length || parsedRows.length < 2) fail('malformed README catalog row')
    const rows = parsedRows.slice(2).map(([, name, root]) => ({ name: name.trim(), root: root.trim() }))
    const catalogPath = value('--catalog')
    const projectRoot = value('--project-root')
    let projects
    try {
      if (catalogPath) {
        const parsed = JSON.parse(readFileSync(resolve(catalogPath), 'utf8'))
        projects = Array.isArray(parsed) ? parsed : parsed.projects
        if (!Array.isArray(projects)) throw new Error('shape')
        for (const project of projects) if (!project?.name || !project?.root || !existsSync(resolve(project.root))) throw new Error(`nonexistent catalog root: ${project?.root}`)
      } else if (projectRoot) {
        const root = resolve(projectRoot)
        if (!existsSync(root)) throw new Error('nonexistent project root')
        let name
        if (existsSync(resolve(root, 'package.json'))) name = JSON.parse(readFileSync(resolve(root, 'package.json'), 'utf8')).name
        else if (existsSync(resolve(root, 'pubspec.yaml'))) name = readFileSync(resolve(root, 'pubspec.yaml'), 'utf8').match(/^name:\s*([^\s#]+)/m)?.[1]
        else for (const file of ['settings.gradle.kts', 'settings.gradle']) if (existsSync(resolve(root, file))) name ??= readFileSync(resolve(root, file), 'utf8').match(/rootProject\.name\s*=\s*['\"]([^'\"]+)/)?.[1]
        name ??= basename(root)
        projects = [{ name, root: projectRoot }]
      } else throw new Error('choose --catalog or --project-root')
    } catch (error) { fail(`invalid catalog shape or input: ${error.message}`); projects = null }
    const duplicate = (items, label) => {
      const seen = new Set(); for (const item of items) { if (seen.has(item.name)) fail(`duplicate ${label} name: ${item.name}`); seen.add(item.name) }
    }
    duplicate(rows, 'README')
    if (projects) {
      duplicate(projects, 'catalog')
      const byName = new Map(rows.map(row => [row.name, row]))
      const catalogNames = new Set(projects.map(project => project.name))
      for (const project of projects) if (!byName.has(project.name)) fail(`missing README project: ${project.name} (${project.root})`)
      else if (byName.get(project.name).root !== project.root) fail(`README project path mismatch: ${project.name} (${byName.get(project.name).root} != ${project.root})`)
      for (const row of rows) if (!catalogNames.has(row.name)) fail(`orphan README project: ${row.name} (${row.root})`)
    }
  }
}

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# scaffold-roadmap.sh — Initialize phase-driven roadmap in a project
#
# Usage: scaffold-roadmap.sh [PROJECT_DIR] [--root <dir>]
#   --root defaults to `roadmap`; `--root docs/roadmap` puts the whole consumer under
#   docs/roadmap/ beside a sibling docs folder. Everything lands UNDER the root, including the
#   schema seam — which is what lets a phase file import `../lib/schema` relatively, with no
#   tsconfig path alias. The legacy toplevel `lib/roadmap/schema.ts` seam stays recognized by
#   cli/lib/roadmap-root.mjs, so existing consumers are untouched.
#
# Creates (<root> = --root, default `roadmap`):
#   <root>/lib/schema.ts     — definePhase() + Zod shapes
#   <root>/lib/registry.ts   — Phase discovery (dynamic import + validation)
#   <root>/lib/emit.ts       — Registry emission (deterministic JSON + digest)
#   <root>/ROADMAP.md        — Validation gate + git strategy
#   <root>/backlog.ts        — Ordered execution queue
#   <root>/phases/           — Empty phases directory
#   reviews/releases/         — Release review reports directory
#   scripts/pre-review.sh     — Automated pre-review checks
#   scripts/build-dashboard.sh — Review dashboard HTML generator

set -euo pipefail

PLUGIN_DIR="$(cd "$(dirname "${BASH_SOURCE[0]}")/.." && pwd)"
PROJECT_DIR="."
ROOT="roadmap"
while [ $# -gt 0 ]; do
  case "$1" in
    --root)
      ROOT="${2:?--root needs a directory}"
      shift 2
      ;;
    --root=*)
      ROOT="${1#--root=}"
      shift
      ;;
    *)
      PROJECT_DIR="$1"
      shift
      ;;
  esac
done

# REFUSE rather than create a second root. Two marked roots is the ambiguity
# cli/lib/roadmap-root.mjs refuses to resolve, so scaffolding one into existence would hand the
# consumer a repo no command can read. A marker is roadmap.config.json or phases/ — the same
# two the resolver probes.
for candidate in roadmap docs/roadmap; do
  [ "$candidate" = "$ROOT" ] && continue
  if [ -f "$PROJECT_DIR/$candidate/roadmap.config.json" ] || [ -d "$PROJECT_DIR/$candidate/phases" ]; then
    echo "scaffold-roadmap: $PROJECT_DIR already carries a roadmap root at $candidate — refusing to create a second one at $ROOT." >&2
    echo "  Two roots means two backlogs and two registries, and every command would refuse to pick between them. Scaffold into $candidate, or move it first." >&2
    exit 1
  fi
done

echo "=== Scaffolding zeroh-roadmap in $PROJECT_DIR (root: $ROOT) ==="

# Create directories
mkdir -p "$PROJECT_DIR/$ROOT/lib"
mkdir -p "$PROJECT_DIR/$ROOT/phases"
mkdir -p "$PROJECT_DIR/reviews/releases"
mkdir -p "$PROJECT_DIR/scripts"

# Copy <root>/lib templates — schema, registry, emit. This is the seam a phase file reaches with
# a RELATIVE `../lib/schema`; no tsconfig `paths` alias is required of the consumer.
for lib_file in schema.ts registry.ts emit.ts; do
  if [ ! -f "$PROJECT_DIR/$ROOT/lib/$lib_file" ]; then
    cp "$PLUGIN_DIR/templates/$lib_file" "$PROJECT_DIR/$ROOT/lib/$lib_file"
    echo "  Created $ROOT/lib/$lib_file"
  else
    echo "  Skipped $ROOT/lib/$lib_file (already exists)"
  fi
done

# Copy ROADMAP.md
if [ ! -f "$PROJECT_DIR/$ROOT/ROADMAP.md" ]; then
  cp "$PLUGIN_DIR/templates/ROADMAP.md" "$PROJECT_DIR/$ROOT/ROADMAP.md"
  echo "  Created $ROOT/ROADMAP.md"
else
  echo "  Skipped $ROOT/ROADMAP.md (already exists)"
fi

# Copy backlog.ts (ordered execution queue)
if [ ! -f "$PROJECT_DIR/$ROOT/backlog.ts" ]; then
  cp "$PLUGIN_DIR/templates/backlog.ts" "$PROJECT_DIR/$ROOT/backlog.ts"
  echo "  Created $ROOT/backlog.ts"
else
  echo "  Skipped $ROOT/backlog.ts (already exists)"
fi

# Scaffold roadmap/arcs/ (OPT-IN — arcs are optional; defineArc rides along via schema.ts).
# Deliberately NOT in audit REQUIRED_ARTIFACTS: a repo without arcs is fully valid.
# The directory only, never an example arc file: anything landing here is a LIVE arc, so a
# copied example makes id A with phases [1] real in a consumer that has authored none.
# templates/example.arc.ts stays installed with the plugin as reference material.
mkdir -p "$PROJECT_DIR/$ROOT/arcs"

# Copy scripts
for script in pre-review.sh build-dashboard.sh generate-changelog-md.ts; do
  if [ ! -f "$PROJECT_DIR/scripts/$script" ]; then
    if [ -f "$PLUGIN_DIR/scripts/$script" ]; then
      cp "$PLUGIN_DIR/scripts/$script" "$PROJECT_DIR/scripts/$script"
      echo "  Created scripts/$script"
    fi
  else
    echo "  Skipped scripts/$script (already exists)"
  fi
done

# Make shell scripts executable
chmod +x "$PROJECT_DIR/scripts/"*.sh 2>/dev/null || true

# Wire the npm scripts the skills invoke. do-phase / plan-phase / full-code-review all run
# `<pm> emit:phases` to regenerate reviews/changelog.json; without this script the agent can't
# find it and skips the regen. Idempotent: existing scripts are left untouched.
if [ -f "$PROJECT_DIR/package.json" ]; then
  node - "$PROJECT_DIR/package.json" "$ROOT" <<'NODE'
const fs = require('fs');
const path = process.argv[2];
const pkg = JSON.parse(fs.readFileSync(path, 'utf8'));
pkg.scripts = pkg.scripts || {};
const root = process.argv[3];
const want = {
  'emit:phases': `tsx ${root}/lib/emit.ts`,
  'changelog:md': 'tsx scripts/generate-changelog-md.ts',
};
let changed = false;
for (const [k, v] of Object.entries(want)) {
  if (!pkg.scripts[k]) { pkg.scripts[k] = v; changed = true; console.log('  Added package.json script: ' + k); }
  else { console.log('  Skipped package.json script ' + k + ' (already set)'); }
}
if (changed) fs.writeFileSync(path, JSON.stringify(pkg, null, 2) + '\n');
NODE
else
  echo "  No package.json found — add a script manually: \"emit:phases\": \"tsx $ROOT/lib/emit.ts\""
fi

echo ""
echo "=== Done ==="
echo ""
echo "Next steps:"
echo "  1. Ensure 'zod' + 'tsx' are in your devDependencies (the emit:phases script runs tsx)."
echo "  2. Regenerate the changelog to confirm wiring: <pm> run emit:phases"
echo "  3. Create your first phase: /plan-phase"
echo "  4. Execute it: /do-phase 1"

---
name: stack-decision
description: Handle requests phrased as choose stack, mobile stack, or compare frameworks by presenting sourced alternatives without defaults and returning an ADR ruling.
---

# Stack decision

Load `references/matrices.md`. Determine which matrices apply from the approved
PRD answers, then present every row in each applicable matrix unchanged.
Not this skill: route initial trigger selection through `using-zeroh-greenfield`, leave repository changes to `greenfield-init` or `brownfield-audit`, and return only `StackDecisionOutput` here. Use `roadmap/arc-evals/phase-30.peval.json` as the 2026-09-04 delivery evidence.

## Selection

Ask exactly one selection question per applicable matrix.
Do not preselect any option before the user answers.
Present the backend matrix ONLY when the PRD answers name an API.

Accept an explicit named option or a request to revisit requirements. Do not
infer a choice from preferences. When the user chooses, ask for or summarize the
reason and confirm it before producing the ruling.
If matrix evidence is unavailable, PRD answers conflict, or the reason is unconfirmed, STOP with `status: unresolved` and name the missing evidence or conflicting answers. Treat selection and STOP behavior as honor-system.

## Callers and ownership

Accept calls from `greenfield-init` for new repositories and from `brownfield-audit` only when stack evidence is unresolved or conflicting. Keep matrices and ADR decision content in this skill and `references/matrices.md`.

Return both stack ADR decisions without implementing design or token values; delegate those values to the selected design system or `zeroh-design`.

## Output

Return one `StackDecisionOutput` containing one object per applicable matrix:

```json
{"status":"decided|unresolved","decisions":[{"adrPath":"docs/adr/0001-tech-stack.md|docs/adr/0002-design-system.md","matrix":"<matrix-heading>","options":["<exact-presented-row>"],"selected":"<named-option>","reason":"<confirmed-reason>","consequences":["<consequence>"],"revisitConditions":["<measurable-condition>"],"rulingDate":"YYYY-MM-DD"}]}
```

Define `YYYY-MM-DD` as the decision's ISO calendar date, `<matrix-heading>` as the literal heading in `references/matrices.md`, and every other placeholder as non-empty text copied or confirmed during selection. On STOP, return `{"status":"unresolved","decisions":[]}` plus the named conflict in the surrounding response.

Accumulate every applicable stack decision in the single
`docs/adr/0001-tech-stack.md`: create a labeled Options group for each presented
matrix, preserve all of its sourced rows, and add one dated ruling per group.
Never replace an earlier group's alternatives or ruling when the next matrix is
answered. Populate `docs/adr/0002-design-system.md` separately from only the
design-system options and ruling.

Add the confirmed consequences and measurable revisit conditions for every
group. Do not write either ADR until the calling workflow's approval gate has
passed.
Treat preservation of earlier groups as honor-system. Treat the no-write rule as enforced by `plugins/zeroh-roadmap/test/fixture-consumer/greenfield-live-evidence.test.mjs` when called inside native initialization; otherwise it is honor-system.
=====
# Stack matrices

Present only the applicable sections and preserve every row when asking for a choice.

## Web
| option | pros | cons | better when | component reuse | source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Next.js + shadcn/ui | Integrated full-stack React and accessible primitives | Framework conventions add coupling | Product needs routing, rendering, and server seams | Registry components remain source-owned | https://nextjs.org/docs |
| Vite + React | Small, fast client toolchain | Backend and routing need separate choices | Client-rendered app has independent services | React components move between Vite applications | https://vite.dev/guide |
| SvelteKit | Concise components and integrated routing | Smaller React-library ecosystem | Team prefers Svelte and server rendering | Svelte components share within Svelte projects | https://svelte.dev/docs/kit |

## Mobile
| option | pros | cons | better when | component reuse | source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Flutter + shadcn_flutter | One Dart UI across supported platforms | Native integrations need platform bridges | Consistent cross-platform UI is primary | Shared Dart widgets and token names | shadcn_flutter |
| Kotlin/Compose/Material 3 | Native Android APIs and tooling | Android-only UI implementation | Android fidelity and platform access dominate | Compose modules and translated token names | https://developer.android.com/compose |
| Expo + @react-native-reusables/cli | React Native workflow with reusable primitives | Native edge cases may require modules | TypeScript skills and multi-platform delivery matter | React Native components and shared token names | @react-native-reusables/cli |

## Monorepo
| option | pros | cons | better when | component reuse | source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| Nx | Project graph, generators, and dependency constraints | More governance concepts | Many projects need enforceable boundaries | Publishable and buildable libraries | https://nx.dev |
| Turborepo | Simple task graph and caching | Fewer architecture constraints | Existing workspace needs lightweight orchestration | Workspace packages | https://turborepo.com/docs |
| pnpm workspaces | Minimal native workspace layer | No project graph or generators | Package linking is the main requirement | Workspace packages | https://pnpm.io/workspaces |

## Library/CLI
| option | pros | cons | better when | component reuse | source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| tsup + node:test | Compact bundling with built-in tests | Two separate tools | Small TypeScript package values minimal test dependencies | Exported modules and fixtures | tsup |
| tsdown + vitest | Modern bundling and rich tests | Additional test dependency | Vite-aligned libraries need fast test ergonomics | Exported modules and test helpers | tsdown |
| unbuild | Convention-led library output | Less explicit build control | Multi-format package follows unjs conventions | Package presets and modules | unbuild |

## Backend
| option | pros | cons | better when | component reuse | source |
| --- | --- | --- | --- | --- | --- |
| NestJS | Structured modules and dependency injection | Heavier framework conventions | Large API needs consistent layering | Modules, guards, and providers | https://docs.nestjs.com |
| Hono | Small web-standard API core | Fewer built-in enterprise patterns | Edge portability and low overhead matter | Handlers and middleware | https://hono.dev/docs |
| Fastify | Mature Node plugin ecosystem and schemas | Node-oriented runtime | Throughput and plugin composition matter | Plugins, schemas, and hooks | https://fastify.dev/docs |

#!/usr/bin/env bash
# capbuild — run a one-off build inside a HARD memory-capped transient cgroup.
#
# Sibling to `slot`. Where `slot` is for long-lived dev servers (soft
# MemoryHigh backpressure, detached service, shows on the pool dashboard),
# `capbuild` is for blocking one-shot builds — SPFx `heft --production`,
# webpack, big tsc — that spike many workers for a few minutes and exit.
#
# Why a separate tool: a build needs a *hard* ceiling, not soft backpressure.
# With MemoryMax set, when the build's worker pool exceeds the cap the kernel
# cgroup OOM killer fires INSIDE the build's own cgroup — the build dies with a
# clean failure, and sibling Claude sessions / dev servers are never touched.
# (On 2026-06-08 a bare `npm run build` in zeroh-spfx ran outside any cgroup
# cap; RAM+swap filled and systemd-oomd killed the fat long-lived Claude
# sessions instead of the short-lived webpack workers. This prevents that.)
#
# This is also the sanctioned way to run a TEST SUITE from the Claude Bash
# tool: the slot-test-guard hook blocks bare `npm test` / `vitest run` /
# `node --test` (no cap → can OOM/swap-thrash the box, cf. 2026-06-11) and
# tells the agent to prefix `capbuild`. There is deliberately no FORCE_BARE
# escape on the agent channel — `capbuild` IS the escape, with a hard cap.
#
# Runs in the FOREGROUND as a --pipe --wait transient service so you see output
# live and get the real exit code — and crucially, capbuild waits OUTSIDE the
# capped cgroup, so an OOM-kill of the run can be detected and surfaced as a
# failure instead of being mistaken for a clean pass.

set -uo pipefail

PROG=capbuild
# Which slice the run is accounted in. Default dev.slice (builds get the 12G
# pool's room). Override to test.slice for test runs you want bound to the
# tight ephemeral-test ceiling (4G), or via CAPBUILD_SLICE in the env.
SLICE="${CAPBUILD_SLICE:-dev.slice}"
MEM_DEFAULT=8G          # hard MemoryMax for the build cgroup
SWAP_DEFAULT=2G         # hard MemorySwapMax (don't let it thrash 15G of swap)
HEAP_DEFAULT=4096       # per-worker V8 --max-old-space-size (MB)

# A transient --user unit inherits the systemd user-manager environment, NOT the
# caller's shell — so scoping knobs (ITEST_FILES, AUDIT_LEDGER_ENABLED, …) die at
# the boundary unless explicitly forwarded. This built-in allowlist of known-safe
# consumer test knobs is auto-forwarded when set. Allowlist-ONLY by design:
# capbuild never blanket-forwards the environment, so secrets (GH_TOKEN, tokens
# in the shell) stay out of the unit. Extend per-run with CAPBUILD_PASS_ENV or
# --env — never by widening this to a wildcard.
DEFAULT_PASS_ENV="ITEST_FILES AUDIT_LEDGER_ENABLED TEST_CONCURRENCY E2E_PROJECT ALLURE"

usage() {
  cat <<EOF
$PROG — run a one-off build in a hard memory-capped cgroup ($SLICE).

Usage:
  $PROG <cmd...>            Run cmd in \$PWD, capped at MemoryMax=$MEM_DEFAULT.
  $PROG --mem 8G <cmd...>   Override hard MemoryMax.
  $PROG --swap 0 <cmd...>   Override hard MemorySwapMax (0 = no swap).
  $PROG --heap 4096 <cmd>   Override per-worker NODE heap cap (MB).
  $PROG --slice test.slice <cmd...>   Account the run in a specific slice
                           (default $SLICE; or set CAPBUILD_SLICE).
  $PROG --env VAR <cmd...>       Forward caller's \$VAR into the capped unit.
  $PROG --env VAR=VAL <cmd...>   Set VAR=VAL inside the unit (repeatable).
  $PROG --lock NAME <cmd...>     Serialize against other $PROG runs holding the
                           same NAME in this working tree (flock; queued runs
                           wait, never fail). Full test tiers auto-lock per-tree;
                           typechecks (tsc / type-check) auto-lock box-wide.
  $PROG --no-lock <cmd...>       Opt out of the auto tier/typecheck lock.
  $PROG --help

Examples:
  cd ~/zeroh-spfx && $PROG npm run build
  $PROG --mem 8G --heap 4096 npm run build
  ITEST_FILES=x.itest.ts $PROG npm run test:integration   # scoped run survives

Env passthrough (a transient unit does NOT inherit your shell env):
  Auto-forwarded when set: $DEFAULT_PASS_ENV
  CAPBUILD_PASS_ENV="A,B"    Forward extra caller vars (comma/space separated).
  --env VAR / --env VAR=VAL  Forward or set one var (repeatable; highest priority).
  Allowlist-only — capbuild never forwards your whole environment (no secrets).

The build runs in the foreground and exits with the command's real code. If it
breaches MemoryMax it is OOM-killed inside its own cgroup — your other sessions
are unaffected. Contrast with \`slot\` (soft cap, detached, for dev servers).
EOF
}

mem="$MEM_DEFAULT"
swap="$SWAP_DEFAULT"
heap="$HEAP_DEFAULT"
env_flags=()            # repeatable --env VAR / --env VAR=VAL specs
lock_name=""            # --lock NAME (explicit serialization group)
no_lock=0               # --no-lock (opt out of the auto tier lock)

while [[ "${1:-}" == --* ]]; do
  case "$1" in
    --mem)   mem="${2:?--mem needs a value}";   shift 2 ;;
    --swap)  swap="${2:?--swap needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
    --heap)  heap="${2:?--heap needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
    --slice) SLICE="${2:?--slice needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
    --env)   env_flags+=("${2:?--env needs a value}"); shift 2 ;;
    --lock)  lock_name="${2:?--lock needs a value}"; shift 2 ;;
    --no-lock) no_lock=1; shift ;;
    --help) usage; exit 0 ;;
    --) shift; break ;;
    *) echo "$PROG: unknown flag '$1'" >&2; exit 2 ;;
  esac
done

[[ $# -gt 0 ]] || { usage; exit 2; }

[[ "$mem"  =~ ^[0-9]+[KMG]?$ ]] || { echo "$PROG: --mem must be a systemd size like '6G' (got '$mem')" >&2; exit 2; }
[[ "$swap" =~ ^[0-9]+[KMG]?$ ]] || { echo "$PROG: --swap must be a systemd size like '2G' or '0' (got '$swap')" >&2; exit 2; }
[[ "$heap" =~ ^[0-9]+$ ]]       || { echo "$PROG: --heap must be MB integer (got '$heap')" >&2; exit 2; }
[[ "$SLICE" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+\.slice$ ]] || { echo "$PROG: --slice must be a slice unit like 'dev.slice' (got '$SLICE')" >&2; exit 2; }
[[ -z "$lock_name" || "$lock_name" =~ ^[A-Za-z0-9_-]+$ ]] || { echo "$PROG: --lock must be [A-Za-z0-9_-]+ (got '$lock_name')" >&2; exit 2; }

# Resolve which caller variables to forward into the capped unit. Three sources,
# LATER WINS: (1) the built-in test-knob allowlist, (2) CAPBUILD_PASS_ENV (comma
# or space separated var NAMES), (3) repeatable --env flags. A bare name is
# forwarded only when actually set in the caller env (an unset knob emits
# nothing); --env VAR=VAL sets an explicit value. Deduped into an associative map
# so each variable produces exactly one --setenv (a later source overrides).
declare -A pass_env=()
for var in $DEFAULT_PASS_ENV ${CAPBUILD_PASS_ENV:+${CAPBUILD_PASS_ENV//,/ }}; do
  # ${!var+x}: set-u-safe "is $var set?" probe via indirection (bare ${!var}
  # would abort under set -u when the named var is unset).
  [[ -n "${!var+x}" ]] && pass_env["$var"]="${!var}"
done
if (( ${#env_flags[@]} )); then
  for spec in "${env_flags[@]}"; do
    if [[ "$spec" == *=* ]]; then
      pass_env["${spec%%=*}"]="${spec#*=}"
    elif [[ -n "${!spec+x}" ]]; then
      pass_env["$spec"]="${!spec}"
    fi
  done
fi
# NODE_OPTIONS is special: capbuild's heap cap MUST stay authoritative (a hard
# ceiling the caller cannot raise is the tool's whole purpose). Take any caller

# so distinguish them by the unit's Result (oom-kill | timeout | signal | ...).
result="$(systemctl --user show "$unit" -p Result --value 2>/dev/null)"
systemctl --user reset-failed "$unit" 2>/dev/null || true

case "$result" in
  oom-kill|timeout|signal|core-dump|watchdog)
    # The run was TERMINATED, not completed — its output is truncated, so a
    # grep for test failures finds nothing and the run looks green. The banner
    # carries the literal tokens those greps look for (`not ok`, `FAIL`) and
    # goes to BOTH stdout and stderr, so the kill surfaces AS a failure through
    # any common output filter. rc is forced non-zero so exit-code checks catch
    # it too.
    if [[ "$result" == oom-kill ]]; then
      why="was OOM-KILLED — it breached MemoryMax=$mem in $SLICE and did NOT finish."
      hint="Re-run with more headroom ($PROG --mem <bigger> $*) or shrink the worker pool (vitest --maxWorkers=2 --pool=forks, node --test-concurrency=2)."
    else
      why="was TERMINATED ($result) and did NOT finish."
      hint="Investigate the cause; do not treat this as a pass."
    fi
    banner="$PROG: not ok / FAIL — the run $why DO NOT treat absent test-failure lines as a pass. $hint"
    printf '%s\n' "$banner"
    printf '%s\n' "$banner" >&2
    [[ $rc -eq 0 ]] && rc=137
    ;;
  *)
    # Ordinary non-zero (e.g. vitest exit 1): the real failure lines are already
    # in the output, so don't inject failure tokens (would skew failure counts);
    # just a stderr note so the non-zero result isn't silently ignored.
    [[ $rc -ne 0 ]] && printf '%s\n' "$PROG: command exited non-zero (code $rc) — treat as a failure, do not proceed as if it passed." >&2
    ;;
esac
exit $rc

#!/bin/bash
# PreToolUse hook for the Bash tool.
#
# The bashrc `pnpm()/next()/vitest()/jest()` wrappers only guard *interactive*
# shells. Claude runs Bash-tool commands via non-interactive `bash -c`, which
# does NOT source ~/.bashrc — so the wrappers never fire on the path that
# OOM'd the box on 2026-06-07 (a Claude session ran a bare `vitest` pool,
# 10.7G, that killed user@1000.service). This hook is the front-line for that
# path: it refuses bare dev-server / test-runner / build invocations and tells
# Claude to route them through `slot`/`capbuild` (→ dev.slice 12G cap).
# (A bare `pnpm build`→`next build` + parallel `tsc --noEmit` swap-thrashed
# every session for ~80min on 2026-06-18 — builds are as heavy as test pools.)
# claude.slice is the
# cgroup catch-all behind it; this hook stops the obvious cases up front.
#
# Design: split the command line into pipeline/list segments and judge each
# independently, AFTER stripping leading env-var assignments, an `env` prefix,
# and any binary path prefix. That closes the cheap bypasses a single anchored
# regex left open (`CI=1 pnpm test`, `./node_modules/.bin/vitest`,
# `slot pnpm dev & pnpm test`).
#
# Allowed:
#   - a segment routed through `slot ...`            (dev.slice, soft cap)
#   - a segment routed through `capbuild ...`        (hard MemoryMax cgroup)
#   - `systemd-run ... --slice=dev|claude|test.slice` (explicitly capped)
#
# NOT allowed — by design there is NO unbounded escape from the Bash tool.
# `FORCE_BARE=1` is honored ONLY by the interactive-shell wrappers in
# ~/.bashrc (a human at a prompt), never here. An autonomous agent in a
# /loop used `FORCE_BARE=1 npm test` as its default path and swap-thrashed
# every session on 2026-06-11 — because the old block message literally
# coached the bypass. The *channel* separates human from agent: humans type
# in an interactive shell, agents arrive through this non-interactive hook.
# So the hatch lives in bashrc; this hook has none. The remediation message
# points at `capbuild`, which gets the agent its test output AND a hard cap.
#
# Fails OPEN if the command can't be read or jq is missing — a guard that
# can't parse must not wedge every Bash call (matches lsp-memory-guard).

INPUT=$(cat)
CMD=$(printf '%s' "$INPUT" | jq -r '.tool_input.command // empty' 2>/dev/null)
[ -z "$CMD" ] && exit 0

# Runner/action fragments (matched after a segment is normalized to start at
# the bare binary name).
PKG_RUNNERS='pnpm|npm|yarn|turbo|bun'
PKG_FLAGS='run|exec|--filter=[^[:space:]]+|-w|--workspace-root|--silent'
PKG_ACTIONS='dev|start|test|test:[^[:space:]]+|build|build:[^[:space:]]+|vitest|jest'
BIN_RUNNERS='vitest|jest|mocha|ava'

# Echoes "x" if the normalized segment $1 is a bare dangerous runner.
_is_bad() {
  local s="$1"
  printf '%s' "$s" | grep -Eq "^($PKG_RUNNERS)([[:space:]]+($PKG_FLAGS))*[[:space:]]+($PKG_ACTIONS)([[:space:]]|\$)" && { echo x; return; }
  printf '%s' "$s" | grep -Eq "^(npx[[:space:]]+)?($BIN_RUNNERS)([[:space:]]|\$)"                                  && { echo x; return; }
  printf '%s' "$s" | grep -Eq "^(npx[[:space:]]+)?playwright[[:space:]]+test([[:space:]]|\$)"                      && { echo x; return; }
  printf '%s' "$s" | grep -Eq "^(npx[[:space:]]+)?cypress[[:space:]]+(run|open)([[:space:]]|\$)"                   && { echo x; return; }
  # node's built-in test runner: `--test` may sit behind loader flags like
  # `--import tsx` (azure_private_agent/office does exactly this), so match
  # `--test`/`--experimental-test` ANYWHERE in the node arg list, not just
  # immediately after `node`. `--test-concurrency=` etc. don't match — the
  # flag must be followed by whitespace or end-of-segment.
  printf '%s' "$s" | grep -Eq "^node[[:space:]].*(--test|--experimental-test)([[:space:]]|\$)"                     && { echo x; return; }
  # tsx running node's test runner, incl. `npx tsx --test` / `npm exec tsx --test`.
  printf '%s' "$s" | grep -Eq "^(npm[[:space:]]+exec[[:space:]]+|npx[[:space:]]+)?tsx[[:space:]].*--test([[:space:]]|\$)" && { echo x; return; }
  # `next dev` (dev server) and `next build` (heavy prod build) both escape into
  # claude.slice when run bare — a bare `pnpm build`→`next build` + parallel
  # `tsc --noEmit` swap-thrashed every session for ~80min on 2026-06-18.
  printf '%s' "$s" | grep -Eq "^(npm[[:space:]]+exec[[:space:]]+|npx[[:space:]]+)?next[[:space:]]+(dev|build)([[:space:]]|\$)" && { echo x; return; }
  # Typecheck: `npm|pnpm|yarn run type-check` / `pnpm typecheck` and bare project
  # `tsc` (`tsc -p …`, `tsc -b`, `tsc --noEmit`). One `type-check` script is an
  # 8-project `tsc` chain — as heavy as a test pool — and N of them across
  # sessions CPU-starved every session on 2026-07-21 (load 47, RAM healthy).
  # Route to `capbuild`, which caps the run AND auto-serializes typechecks under
  # one shared lock so only one runs at a time. `tsc --version|help|init` are
  # trivial and exempt.
  printf '%s' "$s" | grep -Eq "^($PKG_RUNNERS)([[:space:]]+($PKG_FLAGS))*[[:space:]]+type-?check(:[^[:space:]]+)?([[:space:]]|\$)" && { echo x; return; }
  if printf '%s' "$s" | grep -Eq "^tsc([[:space:]]|\$)" \
     && ! printf '%s' "$s" | grep -Eq "^tsc[[:space:]]+--(version|help|init|showConfig)([[:space:]]|\$)"; then
    echo x; return
  fi
}

# Split on && || | ; & into one segment per line (longest operators first).
SEGMENTS=$(printf '%s' "$CMD" | sed -E 's/&&/\n/g; s/\|\|/\n/g; s/[;|&]/\n/g')

DANGER=""
while IFS= read -r seg; do
  # Trim leading subshell/brace punctuation and whitespace.
  seg=$(printf '%s' "$seg" | sed -E 's/^[[:space:](){}]*//')
  [ -z "$seg" ] && continue
  # NOTE: there is deliberately no `FORCE_BARE=1` bypass here. It is stripped
  # as an ordinary leading assignment below, so the underlying command is
  # judged on its merits. The human hatch lives in the interactive bashrc
  # wrappers, not on the agent's Bash-tool channel. (cf. 2026-06-11 incident)
  # Strip leading env-var assignments and an optional `env` prefix.
  while printf '%s' "$seg" | grep -Eq '^([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=[^[:space:]]*[[:space:]]+|env[[:space:]]+)'; do
    seg=$(printf '%s' "$seg" | sed -E 's/^([A-Za-z_][A-Za-z0-9_]*=[^[:space:]]*[[:space:]]+|env[[:space:]]+)//')
  done
  # Strip a path prefix on the binary (./node_modules/.bin/vitest, /usr/bin/node).
  seg=$(printf '%s' "$seg" | sed -E 's#^([^[:space:]]*/)(pnpm|npm|yarn|turbo|bun|vitest|jest|mocha|ava|playwright|cypress|node|next|npx|tsx|tsc)([[:space:]]|$)#\2\3#')
  # Already-capped paths → safe. `slot` → dev.slice (dev servers); `capbuild`
  # → a hard-MemoryMax transient cgroup (one-shot builds/test suites).
  case "$seg" in slot\ *|capbuild\ *) continue ;; esac
  # systemd-run is safe ONLY if it targets a memory-capped slice; a bare
  # `--scope` lands in user.slice uncapped, which is the very escape we guard.
  if printf '%s' "$seg" | grep -Eq '^systemd-run([[:space:]]|$)'; then
    if printf '%s' "$seg" | grep -Eq -- '--slice[ =](dev|claude|test)\.slice'; then continue; fi
    DANGER="$seg"; break
  fi
  if [ -n "$(_is_bad "$seg")" ]; then DANGER="$seg"; break; fi
done <<< "$SEGMENTS"

[ -z "$DANGER" ] && exit 0

REASON='Refusing a bare dev-server / test-runner / typecheck / build from the Bash tool — it runs with no memory cap and can OOM or swap-thrash the box, and typechecks with no serialization CPU-starve every session (a bare vitest pool killed user@1000.service on 2026-06-07; stacked FORCE_BARE test loops froze every session on 2026-06-11; a bare `pnpm build`→`next build` + parallel `tsc --noEmit` swap-thrashed every session for ~80min on 2026-06-18; three concurrent `npm run type-check` chains drove load to 47 and froze every session on 2026-07-21 with RAM healthy). To run a test SUITE, TYPECHECK, or BUILD with a HARD memory cap and real output + exit code, prefix `capbuild`: e.g. `capbuild npm test`, `capbuild npm run type-check`, `capbuild npx tsc -p tsconfig.json --noEmit`, `capbuild node --test src/foo.test.ts`, `capbuild pnpm build`. capbuild auto-serializes typechecks (a shared `typecheck` lock), so concurrent ones queue instead of stampeding — only one runs at a time. For a DEV SERVER use `slot pnpm dev`. There is no unbounded path from the Bash tool by design — `FORCE_BARE=1` is not honored here (it only works for a human at an interactive shell prompt). Use `capbuild` and you get the same result, safely.'
printf '{"decision": "block", "reason": %s}\n' "$(printf '%s' "$REASON" | jq -Rs .)"
exit 0

#!/bin/bash
# PreToolUse hook for the Bash tool — shared-working-tree git hygiene +
# test-tier output integrity. Two rules that were CLAUDE.md prose until
# 2026-07-16, now mechanical (prose is advisory; hooks are deterministic):
#
# 1. Block `git add -A/--all` and `git commit -a/-am/--all`. Up to ~5 Claude
#    sessions share the main checkouts on this box; a blanket stage sweeps a
#    SIBLING session's uncommitted work into your commit (it nearly happened
#    landing ROADCODE 2026-07-15 — seven staged phase files sat in a sibling's
#    conflicted merge index). Stage explicit paths only.
# 2. Block piping a run-tier.sh test tier through truncating filters
#    (tail/head/grep/sed/awk/wc). Truncation eats the failure NAMES and costs
#    a full-tier rerun to recover each one; run-tier.sh already bounds stdout
#    and writes the full TAP stream to .test-logs/. `tee` is allowed (no loss).
#
# Fails OPEN if the command can't be read or jq is missing — a guard that
# can't parse must not wedge every Bash call (matches slot-test-guard).

INPUT=$(cat)
CMD=$(printf '%s' "$INPUT" | jq -r '.tool_input.command // empty' 2>/dev/null)
[ -z "$CMD" ] && exit 0

# Split into statements on && ; || (keep pipes inside a statement — rule 2
# needs to see them). Newlines count as separators too.
STATEMENTS=$(printf '%s' "$CMD" | tr '\n' ';' | sed -E 's/(\&\&|\|\||;)+/\n/g')

DENY=""
while IFS= read -r st; do
  [ -z "$st" ] && continue
  # Rule 1a: git … add … -A/--all   (short -A also inside bundles like -An is
  # not a thing for add; match -A/--all as standalone words)
  if printf '%s' "$st" | grep -Eq '(^|[[:space:]])git([[:space:]]+-C[[:space:]]+[^[:space:]]+)?([[:space:]]+[^[:space:]]+)*[[:space:]]+add([[:space:]]+[^[:space:]]+)*[[:space:]](-A|--all|--no-ignore-removal)([[:space:]]|$)'; then
    DENY="git add -A/--all stages a SIBLING session's uncommitted work on this shared tree. Stage explicit paths only: git add <file> <file>. (Rule: azure_private_agent CLAUDE.md §Shared working tree — mechanically enforced since 2026-07-16.)"
    break
  fi
  # Rule 1b: git … commit with -a / -am / --all (NOT --amend: two dashes + word)
  if printf '%s' "$st" | grep -Eq '(^|[[:space:]])git([[:space:]]+-C[[:space:]]+[^[:space:]]+)?([[:space:]]+[^[:space:]]+)*[[:space:]]+commit([[:space:]]+[^[:space:]]+)*[[:space:]](-a|-am|--all)([[:space:]]|$)'; then
    DENY="git commit -a/-am commits every tracked modification — including a sibling session's dirty files on this shared tree. Stage explicit paths, then commit without -a. (Rule: azure_private_agent CLAUDE.md §Shared working tree — mechanically enforced since 2026-07-16.)"
    break
  fi
  # Rule 2: run-tier.sh … | tail/head/grep/sed/awk/wc  (tee allowed)
  if printf '%s' "$st" | grep -Eq 'run-tier\.sh[^|]*\|[[:space:]]*(tail|head|grep|sed|awk|wc)([[:space:]]|$)'; then
    DENY="NEVER pipe a test tier through tail/head/grep — truncation eats the failure NAMES and costs a full-tier rerun to recover each one. run-tier.sh already bounds stdout (failure names + counts survive) and writes the full TAP stream to .test-logs/<slot>-<ts>.tap — read THAT for diagnostics. Run the tier bare (it self-wraps capbuild); \`| tee file\` is fine if you need a copy."
    break
  fi
done <<< "$STATEMENTS"

[ -z "$DENY" ] && exit 0
printf '{"decision": "block", "reason": %s}\n' "$(printf '%s' "$DENY" | jq -Rs .)"
exit 0
